feed.title: Concept Review: B-SSL (Bitcoin Secure Signing Layer) — Covenant-Free Vault Model Using Taproot, CSV, and CLTV

entry.title: Concept Review: B-SSL (Bitcoin Secure Signing Layer) — Covenant-Free Vault Model Using Taproot, CSV, and CLTV
entry.summary:
The discussion revolves around the technical misuse and misunderstanding of `CSV` (CheckSequenceVerify) as a mechanism for consensus-enforced relative timelocks, particularly in the context of unvaulting transactions. It is emphasized that `CSV` cannot function as a consensus-enforced solution without the integration of presigned transactions. The enforcement of such timelocks is predominantly dependent on the co-signer rather than the protocol itself, with only a minimal time window being truly enforced by consensus.
The ongoing promotion of `CSV` as a fully consensus-enforced method has been identified as misleading. This misrepresentation is significant because it implicates the security protocols intended to safeguard financial assets, potentially leading to false security assurances among users. The critique highlights a repeated attempt to clarify this misconception both privately and publicly, which suggests a persistent challenge in addressing and rectifying this misunderstanding within the community.
